parts.title: A longer text
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I moved to Bristol for work, I hardly knew anyone. I spent most weekends at home until I noticed a community garden behind the library. Volunteers met there every Saturday to grow vegetables. I had never planted anything, but I decided to give it a try.

At first, I worried I would be useless. The other gardeners showed me how to prepare the soil and choose seeds. Soon, I was looking forward to Saturday mornings. We shared the vegetables, but the best part was getting to know people from the neighbourhood.

Six months later, I help welcome new volunteers. Last week, we planned a small café for next summer. It will use food from the garden, and local musicians have offered to play. I’m pleased the project is growing, although I hope we keep the friendly feeling that made me stay.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer first visit the garden?
options: She wanted to try something new.
She was looking for a place to live.
She needed a job at the library.
questions.explanation: She says she had never planted anything but decided to give it a try, because she wanted something new at weekends.

questions.prompt: What was the writer worried about?
questions.explanation: She worried she would be useless, which means she was afraid she could not help.

questions.prompt: What does she say was the best part?
questions.explanation: She says the best part was getting to know people from the neighbourhood.

questions.prompt: What is planned for next summer?
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says a small café with food from the garden and local musicians is planned for next summer.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel about the project growing?
options: She thinks it is becoming too expensive.
She is happy, but wants it to stay welcoming.
She would prefer to leave the garden.
She is proud and wants to start again elsewhere.
questions.explanation: She is pleased the project is growing, but hopes it keeps the friendly feeling.

parts.title: A day without a phone
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Last month, our teacher challenged the class to spend one Saturday without a mobile phone. I thought it would be easy because I rarely use mine. [1] By breakfast, I had already reached for it twice.

I put the phone in a drawer and went to meet my cousin. [2] We walked through the park and talked about our plans for the summer. Later, we visited a bookshop and found a travel guide to the coast.

At lunchtime, I wanted to check the weather. [3] Instead, the shop assistant told us that rain was expected in the afternoon. We bought two cheap umbrellas.

The rain began while we were on the bus home. [4] I noticed that I had been paying more attention to the people around me.

I still use my phone every day, but now I leave it in my bag when I am with friends. [5] The challenge was more useful than I expected.
sentences: It felt strange to arrive without a way to tell her I was late.
Fortunately, we were ready for it.
My cousin has a new phone with a very good camera.
Some people turn their phones off for a whole week.
But I soon discovered how much I depended on it.
My friends say I am better company now.
I decided not to ask anyone for their phone.
We had seen the weather forecast on the shop's television.

gaps.explanation: “But I soon discovered how much I depended on it” contrasts with “I thought it would be easy” and explains “reached for it twice”.
After putting the phone in the drawer and going to meet her cousin, the writer feels strange arriving without a way to tell her she was late.
“I decided not to ask anyone for their phone” follows wanting to check the weather, and “Instead” introduces what the shop assistant said.
“Fortunately, we were ready for it” links the rain with the umbrellas they had just bought.
“My friends say I am better company now” follows leaving the phone in the bag with friends and leads to the conclusion.

parts.title: The weekend project
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: My brother and I decided to [1] a small repair event at our school. We asked people to bring objects that were broken but still [2]. A local electrician kindly [3] to help us. We put up posters so that everyone would know where to [4] their things. On the day, more people came [5] we had expected. We were tired afterwards, but it was a very [6] experience.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: You organise an event; the other verbs do not go with “a small repair event”.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: People brought objects that were broken but still useful, so they could be repaired.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: “Offered to help” is the correct pattern; enjoyed, finished and suggested are followed by -ing.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: People leave their things at a place; you do not borrow, throw or lose them there.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: After “more people came” a comparison needs “than”.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: “Rewarding” means giving satisfaction, which fits being tired but happy.

parts.title: A note from the coast
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Ben,
We arrived [1] the coast yesterday evening. The hotel is smaller [2] I expected, but our room has a wonderful view. We have already visited the old harbour, [3] we are going to take a boat trip tomorrow. If the weather [4] good, we’ll walk along the cliffs afterwards. I’ve never seen [5] many seabirds before! I’ll send you some photos when we get [6] home.
Love,
Mia

gaps.explanation: We say “arrive at” a place such as the coast.
“Smaller than I expected” is a comparison.
“And” adds a second plan to the one already done.
A condition in the present uses the present simple: “If the weather is good”.
“So many” goes before plural countable nouns such as seabirds.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Are we still meeting at the café at half past ten?

turns.speaker: kofi
turns.text: I was just about to call you. I walked past it and there’s a sign on the door. It’s closed for the whole week.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Oh no. Shall we try the station, then? There’s a coffee stand near the ticket office.

turns.speaker: kofi
turns.text: Hmm, it’s always packed on Saturdays. We’d never find a seat.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: True. Well, what about that little bookshop on Mill Street, the one with cushions upstairs? They sell drinks too.

turns.speaker: kofi
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll wait outside for you.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Great. See you at half past ten.

question.explanation: Dana suggests the station, but Kofi says it is always packed, so they agree on the little bookshop on Mill Street instead of the closed café.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Attention please. This announcement is for passengers waiting for the station bus. The bus normally leaves at twenty past ten, but today it is running late because of roadworks. Earlier, a driver told us it would arrive by ten thirty-five, but that was before another delay on the bridge. The bus will now leave at quarter to eleven. Please stay at the stop and don’t wait in the car park, because the bus will not stop there. Tickets from the machine are still valid. Thank you for your patience, and we are sorry for the trouble.

question.prompt: What time does the bus leave?
question.explanation: The normal time was twenty past ten and the driver’s guess was ten thirty-five, but because of the second delay the bus will leave at quarter to eleven.

turns.speaker: ravi
turns.text: Are you walking to college today, Ines?

turns.speaker: ines
turns.text: I was going to go on foot. It only takes twenty minutes. But look at that rain.

turns.speaker: ravi
turns.text: You could borrow my bicycle. It’s in the garage.

turns.speaker: ines
turns.text: Thanks, but I nearly fell off it last time. The brakes are terrible.

turns.speaker: ravi
turns.text: Fair enough. It is a bit old.

turns.speaker: ines
turns.text: I’ll get on the number six bus. It stops right outside my house.

turns.speaker: ravi
turns.text: It’ll be crowded, though.

turns.speaker: ines
turns.text: I don’t mind. I’ll just listen to music.

question.explanation: Ines was going to walk, but it is raining. She refuses Ravi’s old bicycle because of the brakes and says she will get on the number six bus.

turns.speaker: carmen
turns.text: Did you buy the blue jacket in the end?

turns.speaker: joel
turns.text: I nearly did. Then the assistant showed me the label, and it isn’t waterproof. We’ll be walking in the hills for three days.

turns.speaker: carmen
turns.text: Oh, that’s true. Was there anything else?

turns.speaker: joel
turns.text: There’s a green one next to it. It’s a bit more expensive, but it’s really warm.

turns.speaker: carmen
turns.text: Maybe neither jacket is worth it. You could wait for the sale.

turns.speaker: joel
turns.text: The sale doesn’t start until next month, and the trip is in two weeks. I’ll go back tomorrow and get the heavier one.

question.explanation: Joel nearly bought the blue jacket, but it is not waterproof. He decides to go back for the heavier, warmer green one rather than wait for the sale.

turns.speaker: pablo
turns.text: We could go swimming after work.

turns.speaker: nora
turns.text: I’d love to, but I left my kit at my sister’s. And honestly, I’m tired.

turns.speaker: pablo
turns.text: Shopping, then? I need a birthday present for my mum.

turns.speaker: nora
turns.text: The shops close at six. We’d never make it.

turns.speaker: pablo
turns.text: Right. Then let’s take a walk along the river. It’s light until eight.

turns.speaker: nora
turns.text: Good idea. I could do with some fresh air.

turns.speaker: pablo
turns.text: I’ll bring a sandwich and a flask of tea. There’s a bench by the bridge where we can sit for a while.

turns.speaker: nora
turns.text: Lovely. Let’s meet at the gate at half past five.

question.prompt: What will they do after work?
question.explanation: Swimming is impossible because Nora left her kit, and the shops close at six, so Pablo suggests a walk along the river and Nora agrees.

turns.speaker: yuki
turns.text: Hi, I’d like to check if the museum is open on Mondays.

turns.speaker: clerk
turns.text: It normally is, yes. But I’m afraid tomorrow is different.

turns.speaker: yuki
turns.text: Oh? Is it because the staff are away? Last year it closed for a staff holiday.

turns.speaker: clerk
turns.text: That was in August. And it isn’t because it’s quiet, either. We’ve had lots of visitors this month.

turns.speaker: yuki
turns.text: So what’s the problem?

turns.speaker: clerk
turns.text: Builders are coming to fix the roof in the main hall. They say the repairs will take two days.

turns.speaker: yuki
turns.text: I see. When does it reopen?

turns.speaker: clerk
turns.text: Wednesday morning at nine.

question.prompt: Why is the museum closed tomorrow?
question.explanation: The clerk says the staff holiday was in August and visitor numbers are high, but builders are coming to fix the roof and the repairs will take two days.

turns.speaker: oscar
turns.text: Could I have the soup, please?

turns.speaker: greta
turns.text: Sorry, we’ve run out. The chef is making more, but it won’t be ready for half an hour.

turns.speaker: oscar
turns.text: Hmm, that’s too long. A salad, then?

turns.speaker: greta
turns.text: Of course. Though the dressing has nuts in it.

turns.speaker: oscar
turns.text: I’m allergic, so I’d better not.

turns.speaker: greta
turns.text: Then I’d suggest the pie. It’s the vegetable one, with mushrooms and spinach, and it comes with potatoes.

turns.speaker: oscar
turns.text: Does it contain any fish?

turns.speaker: greta
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: oscar
turns.text: Great. I’ll have that, please.

question.explanation: The soup has run out and the salad dressing has nuts, which Oscar cannot eat, so he accepts the pie with mushrooms and spinach.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: tariq
turns.text: How was the concert?

turns.speaker: maeve
turns.text: The band was great, honestly better than I expected.

turns.speaker: tariq
turns.text: Better than the last one?

turns.speaker: maeve
turns.text: Much better. But the tickets, forty pounds!

turns.speaker: tariq
turns.text: That’s what I paid last time, and it seemed fair.

turns.speaker: maeve
turns.text: Yes, I don’t mind the price. What I minded was the hall. You couldn’t move. I stood behind a pillar for two hours.

turns.speaker: tariq
turns.text: Same for me last year. They should sell fewer tickets.

turns.speaker: maeve
turns.text: Exactly. All those people! I’d go again if it were somewhere bigger.

question.prompt: What do Maeve and Tariq agree about?
options: The band was better than expected
question.explanation: Maeve says she does not mind the price and liked the band; what annoyed her was the hall, and Tariq agrees that too many tickets are sold for all those people.

turns.speaker: selma
turns.text: Still working on the report?

turns.speaker: adam
turns.text: Yes, it’s due tomorrow at nine.

turns.speaker: selma
turns.text: Do you want me to read it? You sound worried.

turns.speaker: adam
turns.text: A bit, to be honest, but not about the writing. The text is done. I just need to check a few figures against last year’s.

turns.speaker: selma
turns.text: Then you’ll be ready by tonight.

turns.speaker: adam
turns.text: Easily. Mr Lang did ask me to add a section yesterday, which was annoying, but it was only one page.

turns.speaker: selma
turns.text: Well, I’m glad it’s under control.

turns.speaker: adam
turns.text: Me too. I should finish before dinner, and then I’m going home to sleep.

question.prompt: How does Adam feel about his report?
options: Sure he can finish it in time
Unhappy with what he has written
Annoyed that his manager changed the plan
question.explanation: Adam says the text is done and only a few figures need checking, so he expects to finish before dinner; the extra page was annoying but small.

turns.speaker: lucy
turns.text: Shall we take the car to Bath?

turns.speaker: kai
turns.text: Parking is awful there, and petrol is expensive.

turns.speaker: lucy
turns.text: Okay. What about the coach? It’s the cheapest, only eight pounds.

turns.speaker: kai
turns.text: But it takes two and a half hours with all the stops.

turns.speaker: lucy
turns.text: True. The train is quicker, but it costs more.

turns.speaker: kai
turns.text: I don’t mind paying a bit extra if I can read and not worry about traffic.

turns.speaker: lucy
turns.text: Same here. I might even sleep.

turns.speaker: kai
turns.text: Then let’s book the ten o’clock one.

question.prompt: What do Lucy and Kai agree about the trip to Bath?
options: The car would be the cheapest way
The train is the best choice
question.explanation: Both reject the car because of parking and petrol, and the coach because of the long journey; they agree to pay extra to go by train and book the ten o’clock one.

turns.speaker: ian
turns.text: I want to get better at taking photos. Should I do an evening course?

turns.speaker: beth
turns.text: They cost two hundred pounds, and you just sit and listen.

turns.speaker: ian
turns.text: Hmm. Or should I buy a proper camera?

turns.speaker: beth
turns.text: I did that, and my pictures weren’t any better, honestly. My phone is fine. What helped was the Thursday group at the library. You go out together and everyone shows what they took.

turns.speaker: ian
turns.text: Do they mind beginners?

turns.speaker: beth
turns.text: Not at all. You get comments straight away from other people, and it’s free.

turns.speaker: ian
turns.text: That sounds better than a classroom. I’ll come on Thursday.

question.prompt: What is Beth's opinion about learning photography?
question.explanation: Beth rejects the expensive course and the new camera, and says the free Thursday group helped because everyone shows photos and gives comments.

turns.speaker: rosie
turns.text: Hi, I bought these last week, but they’re a bit tight.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Are they uncomfortable, or is there a problem with them?

turns.speaker: rosie
turns.text: They’re fine. No marks, nothing broken. Can I just get my money back?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: We’d be happy to refund you, but the sale has ended, so I can only give you a voucher.

turns.speaker: rosie
turns.text: Oh. I’d rather have shoes.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: We have a bigger size in the same style. Let me check the back.

turns.speaker: rosie

question.explanation: Rosie says nothing is broken and she would rather have shoes than a voucher; the assistant offers the same style in a bigger size and she asks him to check.

turns.speaker: neil
turns.text: How was the picnic?

turns.speaker: wendy
turns.text: Mixed. It started sunny, then dark clouds came.

turns.speaker: neil
turns.text: Did you go home?

turns.speaker: wendy
turns.text: Eventually, but first we sat in the car and ate the sandwiches. It was funny. I thought Ben had forgotten the drinks, but they were in the boot.

turns.speaker: neil
turns.text: So was it a waste of a day?

turns.speaker: wendy
turns.text: No, I’m happy we didn’t cancel. Whatever the weather did, we had a lovely hour before the rain. The picnic in the car was a laugh.

turns.speaker: neil
turns.text: Sounds better than my day.

question.prompt: How does Wendy feel about the picnic?
options: Annoyed that they had to leave
Pleased they went despite the weather
Embarrassed that Ben forgot the drinks
question.explanation: Wendy says she is happy they did not cancel, because they had a lovely hour before the rain and the picnic in the car was fun.

parts.title: A talk about a nature club
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to this evening’s meeting. I’m Priya, and I help to run the Green Steps nature club. Let me tell you what we do and how you can take part. First, the timing. We used to meet on Sunday afternoons, but so few people could come that we changed it. Now we gather every Saturday morning at nine o’clock, and nobody has to stay all day. Next, the place. Some people think we start at the main gate on Church Road, but that’s wrong. We meet at the lake entrance of West Park, and you’ll see a green flag. Our next project is to clean the river path, which gets very muddy. So please wear old shoes. You don’t need walking boots, because they’re too heavy for that path. We’ll provide gloves and bags. Bring a bottle of water, because we’ll be outside for about three hours. Please don’t bring juice, because it brings wasps. At midday we’ll stop for lunch. Last year we ate in the garden, but it rained, so this time we’ve booked the community room at the sports centre. Everyone brings something to share, and there’ll be tea and coffee. In the afternoon, we count the birds along the river and write down what we see. We send the numbers to a national survey, which is a lot of fun. Finally, membership. Normally it costs twenty pounds a year, and the new term starts in April. But if you join before the end of March, it’s free. Just give me your name at the end of this meeting. Thank you very much, and I hope to see you on Saturday.

gaps.prompt: The group meets once a week, on ___ mornings
gaps.explanation: Priya says they used to meet on Sunday afternoons, but now they gather every Saturday morning.

gaps.prompt: Meeting point: the lake entrance of ___
gaps.explanation: She says the main gate on Church Road is wrong; they meet at the lake entrance of West Park.

gaps.prompt: Footwear for the river path: ___ that can get dirty
gaps.explanation: She asks for old shoes and says walking boots are too heavy.
Priya asks everyone to bring a bottle of water and says juice brings wasps.

gaps.prompt: Lunch will be in the ___ at the sports centre
gaps.explanation: The garden was used last year, but this time they booked the community room.

gaps.prompt: Joining is free if you apply before the end of ___
gaps.explanation: Membership normally costs twenty pounds, but it is free before the end of March; April is when the new term starts.

parts.title: An interview with a young chef
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Ella, you’re one of the youngest head chefs in the city. When did you first get interested in cooking?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: Quite early, actually. My grandmother had a big garden, and I spent a lot of time there, but honestly I found pulling up carrots a bit boring. What I loved was her kitchen on Sundays, when she let me help with the dough. I must have been eight. Her bread was famous in the village. I didn’t read cookbooks, because she never used one. It was all in her head.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: But you didn’t go straight into a kitchen after school, did you?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: No. I studied science at university, and I’d love to say it was my own idea. It wasn’t a plan to become a doctor or anything like that, and I didn’t need it for a job either. My parents just kept telling me it would keep my options open, and I trusted them. I’m glad now, because I understand why food behaves the way it does.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you find your first job in a professional kitchen?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: That was harder than I expected. I had put my CV on a few websites, and I’d noticed an advert for a kitchen assistant, but I never heard back. My old teacher offered to make a phone call, but I wanted to do it on my own. In the end my friend Marta, who was washing dishes at a small hotel, told me they needed someone on Saturdays, and that’s how I started.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did the hotel teach you?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: Mostly that you can’t stand still. We served two hundred breakfasts on a busy morning, and I had to keep up. I didn’t learn anything about managing the place, because that was the owner’s job, and I never helped with the menu either. But after six months I could work faster than anyone my age.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you enjoy most about it these days?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: Well, finishing early would be nice, but that never happens in a restaurant! And yes, I work with my cousin, though that wasn’t why I chose this place. The best moment is when I look through the little window and see people smiling at something I invented that morning.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What would you say to someone who is just starting out?

turns.speaker: ella
turns.text: Don’t spend your savings on expensive knives. I used a cheap one for years. You can follow recipes at first, but don’t be afraid to ignore them later. The thing is to keep cooking, even when it goes wrong. I burnt so many dinners, and each of my mistakes taught me something.

questions.prompt: What did Ella enjoy doing with her grandmother?
questions.explanation: Ella says she loved her grandmother’s kitchen and helping with the dough; the bread was famous, while she found the garden boring and her grandmother never used a cookbook.

questions.prompt: Why did Ella study science?
options: It was needed for a café job
She wanted to become a doctor
questions.explanation: Ella says science was not for a job or to become a doctor; her parents kept telling her it would keep her options open.

questions.prompt: How did Ella get her first kitchen job?
options: A friend told her about it
questions.explanation: Her teacher offered to help and an advert got no reply, but her friend Marta told her the hotel needed someone on Saturdays.

questions.prompt: What did she learn at the hotel?
questions.explanation: Ella says she did not learn management or menus; the hotel taught her to keep up and work faster.

questions.prompt: What does Ella enjoy most about her work?
questions.explanation: Ella says the best moment is seeing people smiling at something she invented; finishing early never happens and working with her cousin was not the reason.

questions.prompt: What advice does Ella give beginners?
questions.explanation: Ella says that she burnt many dinners and that each of her mistakes taught her something, while expensive knives and recipes are not necessary.
